protocol: Independent review under D-000; refute not confirm; Route B scoped preview threat model for DR-003, architecture-preview scope
summary: The two axes the prompt names for this artifact both come back clean, and I checked them by arithmetic rather than by reading. The actor split is named and correctly bounded: it states adopted D-032's rule that host-under-instruction is outside DR-105 and component tails stay in DR-105, that host doctor acts are unexercisable until the host-effect contract is recorded by the joint owners, and — the part that matters — that this TM names that split and does not replace that contract. Wave-through is rejected in a dedicated field and defeated in substance by seven enumerated boundaries whose count field matches the array, whose families match adopted D-030's seven verbatim, and whose trust sub-assets match D-030's parenthetical seven verbatim. The open frame is genuinely open and carries a rule I have not seen elsewhere in this corpus: 'A D-002 successor that adds a boundary adds an owed row here; silence is not coverage.' One advisory, the same missing foreclosure clause I raised on the sibling DR-008 disposition.

findings.claim: The condition-1 clause forecloses self-recording by existence but not by independent review, where the sibling DR-005 disposition in the same dispatch forecloses both. The omitted route is live, because this review is issuing an ACCEPT on the artifact.
findings.evidence: condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded reads in part: 'This file existing is not owner recording. It does not authorize a security-complete claim.' The parallel clause in route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v1 at 6d33037cd2ffbb6080ac359aa2b87a8b3f1c2edc0fe4210291792285263f67ce reads: 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording.' The three dispositions in this dispatch are built to one template, so the difference is an omission rather than a distinction. It is sharper here than on the DR-008 sibling for a reason specific to this row: file 08 names the V1 coordinator as a co-owner of DR-003, and the artifact correctly draws the consequence — 'the coordinator may record jointly; it does not replace that authority.' A row where the coordinator is genuinely half the owner is the row where the boundary between drafting, reviewing and recording is easiest to blur, so the clause that keeps a review from counting as the recording is the one most worth having here. Nothing in the artifact is false; the clause is simply narrower than its sibling's.
findings.proposedFix: Adopt the DR-005 wording: 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording.' Keep the existing security-complete sentence alongside it.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 937c852a0ed6d3dbf2542a0025e190ec9128e2e0dcb7b0b166ac3f04098462a9 both times. No drift.

The actor split is not omitted, which is the axis the prompt names for this artifact. actorSplitNamed cites adopted D-032 as its source and states the rule: 'Host-under-instruction is outside DR-105. Component tails stay in DR-105. Host doctor acts are unexercisable until the host-effect contract is recorded by the joint owners. This TM names that split; it does not replace that contract.' All four clauses match adopted D-032, and the last is the one that keeps the TM from over-reaching into the host-effect contract's territory — a boundary the host-effect lineage spent eight versions establishing.

Wave-through is rejected and the rejection is substantive, not verbal. waveThroughRejected states that a disposition saying only 'preview needs no TM' is rejected, cites D-030's own rejection, and points at the enumeration. The enumeration then does the work: seven boundaries with ids B-CMD, B-IN, B-PROC, B-STATE, B-OUT, B-PLAT and B-TRUST.

The boundary arithmetic holds and matches its governing decision exactly. boundaryCount is 7 and the boundaries array holds 7. familiesNamedByD030 lists command, input, process/protocol, state, output, platform and trust — seven, and identical to adopted D-030's enumeration 'command, input, process/protocol, state, output, platform, and trust'. trustSubAssetsNamedByD030 lists hostile repository/source, parser/provider admission, four-platform matrix, first-install trust, doctor, signed delivery and Node closure — seven, and identical to D-030's parenthetical. The seven boundary ids map one-to-one onto the seven families. No family is dropped and none is invented.

The frame is genuinely open rather than a closed list wearing an open label. openFrame reads 'Every boundary D-002 ships, including but not limited to the families below. A D-002 successor that adds a boundary adds an owed row here; silence is not coverage.' The second sentence is stronger than the open-frame language elsewhere in this corpus: it converts the openness into a standing obligation on future D-002 successors rather than leaving it as a disclaimer, which forecloses the reading that an unenumerated boundary is thereby out of scope.

Nothing settled is pretended. whatMustNotBePretendedSettled and whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA keep V10, custody, G19 and the publication block on Route A, and the honesty field records that the full-TM constraint remains true 'for any claim wider than the architecture preview'. The condition-1 clause adds a fourth guard specific to this row: 'It does not authorize a security-complete claim.'

The coordinator is not treated as the sole owner, and the co-ownership case is handled correctly. ownerWhoMustRecord reads 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator (file 08 DR-003). Coordinator may draft. D-000 does not make the coordinator Threat-model authority. File 08 names V1 coordinator as co-owner: the coordinator may record jointly; it does not replace that authority.' That matches file 08's DR-003 owner cell exactly and matches the construction adopted D-032 and the host-effect contract both use for this row.

No silent SATISFIED: two occurrences, both negative — the authority claim's 'records nothing as SATISFIED' and whatThisDoesNotDo's 'Does not mark DR-003 SATISFIED.' Header carries CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, DO-NOT-SEAL and binds NOTHING.
Implementation is not authorized: the single occurrence of docs/v2/implementation/ is inside the condition-5 preservation clause.

verdictNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES. Both named axes hold and I tested them by arithmetic against adopted D-030 rather than by reading the claim: seven boundaries, seven families, seven trust sub-assets, all matching the governing decision verbatim with nothing dropped or invented. The open-frame rule that a later D-002 boundary 'adds an owed row here; silence is not coverage' is the strongest sentence in the artifact and I would keep it verbatim. The single advisory is the same one-clause omission I raised on the DR-008 sibling, and it bites slightly harder here because the coordinator is a named co-owner of this row, which is exactly where drafting, reviewing and recording are easiest to blur.
